catalogMeta.label: Compare Conditions
catalogMeta.description: Compare matched ramp setups that change one variable and identify which condition reduces the required push.

fullData.title: Friction Friction! Moving Boxes
fullData.description: Experiment with different surface materials to see how much push force is needed to move a box up the ramp.

challenges.title: Wheel or Box?
challenges.brief: The loads have the same weight and climb the same ramp. Which setup needs less push?
challenges.hint: Rolling contact usually resists motion less than a sliding surface.
challenges.explainOnSolve: The wheel has less resistance, so less of the push is spent overcoming friction.

challenges.title: Steep or Gentle?
challenges.brief: Everything is identical except the ramp angle. Which setup needs less push?
challenges.hint: Ask how much gravity points back down each ramp.
challenges.explainOnSolve: On the gentler ramp, a smaller part of gravity pulls the load downhill, so the required push is lower.

challenges.title: Rough or Smooth?
challenges.brief: The box, weight, and angle stay fixed. Which surface needs less push?
challenges.hint: Friction pushes against sliding motion.
challenges.explainOnSolve: The smooth surface produces less friction, leaving more of the applied force available to move the box.

challenges.title: Choose the Easier Route
challenges.brief: The barrel and surface are unchanged. Which route needs less push?
challenges.hint: Compare the slopes, not the drawing labels or positions.
challenges.explainOnSolve: The gentler route reduces the downhill component of gravity, so it needs less input force.

query.topic: Investigate how surface friction changes the push needed to move a box

catalogMeta.label: Find the Threshold
catalogMeta.description: Use controlled trials to find the smallest push setting that makes a fixed load climb.

fullData.title: Friction Challenge!
fullData.description: Test different surface materials to see how surface friction changes the push needed to move a box up the ramp.

challenges.title: Find the First Moving Force
challenges.brief: Find the smallest push setting that makes the wheel climb. Test carefully -- a larger force works, but is not the answer.
challenges.hint: Start low, then narrow the gap between a force that fails and one that works.
challenges.explainOnSolve: You found the threshold: the first slider step where push becomes greater than gravity plus friction.

challenges.title: Measure the Threshold
challenges.brief: Find the least push that starts this crate moving uphill.
challenges.hint: Use failed tests as evidence. Increase by smaller amounts when you get close.
challenges.explainOnSolve: At the threshold, your push just exceeds the two forces opposing motion: downhill gravity and friction.

challenges.title: Test a Steeper Ramp
challenges.brief: Measure the smallest push that will move the barrel up this steeper ramp.
challenges.hint: A steep ramp sends more of gravity down the ramp, even when friction is low.
challenges.explainOnSolve: The steeper angle raised the threshold because more of the barrel's weight acted downhill.

challenges.title: Test a Rough Surface
challenges.brief: Find the minimum push for this rough-surface setup.
challenges.hint: Both the slope and the rough surface oppose your push.
challenges.explainOnSolve: This threshold includes both downhill gravity and the larger friction force from the rough surface.

catalogMeta.label: Design with a Force Budget
catalogMeta.description: Hold the platform height fixed and design the steepest whole-degree ramp that stays within a force budget.

fullData.title: Surface Friction Loading Dock Challenge
fullData.description: Experiment with different surface frictions to see how much push force is needed to move a box up the ramp.

challenges.title: Loading Dock Limit
challenges.brief: Build the steepest whole-degree ramp this push budget can handle. The dock height must stay fixed.
challenges.hint: If the load cannot climb, make the ramp gentler. If it can, see whether one more degree still works.
challenges.explainOnSolve: You found the boundary design: any steeper would exceed the force budget, while any gentler would use more ramp length than necessary.

challenges.title: Smooth Access Ramp
challenges.brief: Use the available push to make the steepest workable ramp to the fixed platform.
challenges.hint: Search for the boundary between works and does not work, then choose the steepest working angle.
challenges.explainOnSolve: The design balances two constraints: enough push to climb and no extra ramp length beyond what the budget requires.

challenges.title: Rough-Site Ramp
challenges.brief: The site surface is rough. Find the steepest ramp that still reaches the platform within the force budget.
challenges.hint: Roughness uses part of the force budget before the load even fights the slope.
challenges.explainOnSolve: Because friction consumed more of the budget, this design needed a gentler, longer ramp.

challenges.title: Barrel Delivery Route
challenges.brief: Choose the steepest whole-degree route the crew can use without exceeding its push limit.
challenges.hint: Try a working angle, then increase one degree at a time until the next step fails.
challenges.explainOnSolve: The last working angle is the efficient boundary: it reaches the same height with the shortest feasible ramp.
